title: Cisco ISE Data Connect — DB-Direct Query Audit and Slow-Query Detection
exclusions: Does not replace enterprise SIEM correlation for unrelated threat classes. Does not constitute legal, regulatory, or executive attestation for 'Cisco ISE Data Connect — DB-Direct Query Audit and Slow-Query Detection'. Does not cover entities explicitly scoped out in operational_exceptions.csv. Pair with sibling UCs in the same subcategory when the SPL surface alone cannot prove control effectiveness (see prerequisiteUseCases on UC-17.1.58).
evidence: Saved search uc_17_1_58_cisco_ise_data_connect_db_direct_query_a, dashboard panel tied to this UC, weekly CSV export archived to index=evidence with change-ticket reference, and git-tracked lookup baselines referenced in the search.

compliance.assurance_rationale: PCI 10.2.2 — audit logging of admin actions; Data Connect direct DB access requires logging.
ITGC logical access — DB-direct access is privileged.

compliance.controlObjective: Database-access logging evidence for ISE Data Connect read-only consumers.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Run a deliberately heavy query via Data Connect (`SELECT * FROM mnt_radius_auth WHERE rownum > 1000000`). Query takes 60s. UC-17.1.58 fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Run a normal query that completes in 2s. UC-17.1.58 does not fire.

dataSources: ISE Data Connect (introduced ISE 3.2) provides direct read-only Oracle connectivity to MnT data. Audit/connection events emitted in *Administrative and Operational Audit* category — codes `52100` (Data Connect login), `52101` (Data Connect login failure), `52110` (Data Connect slow query). Query details may be captured at the consumer side (e.g. Splunk DB Connect) — `index=splunkdbx sourcetype=splunkdbx:db_query`. ISE OpenAPI exposes Data Connect status via `/api/v1/dataconnect/status`. Field: `db_user`, `query_duration_ms`, `query_text`.
app: `Splunk Add-on for Cisco Identity Services` ([Splunkbase 1915](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1915)) + `Splunk DB Connect` for the consumer side.
spl:
(index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" MessageCode IN (52100, 52101, 52110))
  OR (index=splunkdbx sourcetype="splunkdbx:db_query" "jdbc:oracle:thin:@//ise-mnt:2484")
| stats count, count(eval(MessageCode=="52101")) as login_failures, count(eval(MessageCode=="52110" OR query_duration_ms > 30000)) as slow_queries, max(query_duration_ms) as max_duration by db_user
| where login_failures > 5 OR slow_queries > 0 OR max_duration > 60000
description: Audits Data Connect direct DB access events and detects login failures (potential brute-force) AND slow queries (>30s) that may degrade ISE platform performance.
value: Data Connect provides huge analytical value but exposes the MnT Oracle DB directly. Brute-force on the DB account or runaway slow queries can degrade the platform. Auditing protects the integration value while bounding the risk.
implementation: Confirm *Administrative and Operational Audit* at INFO. If using Splunk DB Connect, ensure DB Connect is logging query details. Schedule every 30 min.
visualization: (1) Single value: slow queries last 1h. (2) Top-N: queries by duration. (3) Login-failure trend.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance windows** — Planned change activity in the CMDB or change calendar produces expected deviations that match this detection pattern during approved maintenance. Cross-check ServiceNow change records for `state=implement` and the affected CI list.

2. **Backup and batch job cycles** — Nightly ETL, backup agents, or log rotation jobs generate bursts of similar events that resemble alert conditions but occur on a fixed schedule. Compare `_time` against the documented batch window before paging.

3. **Onboarding and provisioning bursts** — New users, devices, or services provisioned in bulk can temporarily skew counts until baselines stabilize. Filter events tagged `onboarding=true` in the identity or asset lookup.

4. **Monitoring and health-check traffic** — Synthetic transactions or internal scanner accounts generate probe traffic designed to exercise the control. Exclude service accounts listed in `monitoring_exceptions.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** Maintain a KV Store lookup `operational_exceptions.csv` with columns `entity`, `exception_reason`, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, and `approved_by`. Join the saved search to this lookup and filter `where isnull(exception_reason) OR now() > valid_until` so approved windows suppress alerts without muting the search globally.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• ISE Data Connect enabled (Administration > System > Settings > Data Connect).
• Splunk DB Connect or another consumer.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable *Administrative and Operational Audit* at INFO.

Step 2 — Create the search
Search in `spl` field. Schedule every 30 min.

Step 3 — Validate
Provoke as above.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard "ISE — Data Connect Audit":
• Slow-query count.
• Top-N queries.
• Login-failure trend.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **Slow queries from analytics workload** — Coordinate to schedule outside peak.
• **Login failures from one host** — Brute-force or stale credential cache.
• **No DB Connect events** — DB Connect not configured to log queries.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk Add-on for Cisco Identity Services` ([Splunkbase 1915](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1915)) + `Splunk DB Connect` for the consumer side.). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog, splunkdbx:db_query into nac, splunkdbx. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`db_user, login_failures, max_duration, query_duration_ms`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: ISE allows a special direct-to-database connection for big reports. We watch who's connecting and how long their queries take — slow queries can slow down ISE itself, and many failed logins can mean someone's trying to crack a password.
